text:
mike: Quick sync — ran into a nasty oscillation with dedicated pools + preemptible spillover during sustained burst. Headroom gets consumed, autoscaler spins up preemptible nodes, tenant workloads get evicted, traffic drops, autoscaler tears down, repeat. Anyone seen this pattern?
anya: Yup saw similar in staging last week. Root cause felt like the admission logic treats preemptible capacity as equivalent headroom. We need differentiation in the admission surface. :thinking_face:
leo: I think the core issue is the admission window + burst accounting. If preemptible comes online quickly it looks like real capacity to the tenant quota system. We should mark preemptible as 'transient' so admission discounts it for X minutes.
sophia: Agree. Idea: introduce a short stabilization window after preemptible nodes register where their contribution to available headroom is weighted (e.g., 0.2 -> ramps to 1.0 over 60s). That avoids immediate eviction loops.
mike: That would help. Also worried about SLOs — some tenants prefer low-latency and would rather be declined than routed to preemptible. Need a policy switch per-tenant.
anya: +1 per-tenant QoS flag. Default behavior: conservative (don't count preemptible for latency-sensitive). Allow opt-in for cost-sensitive workloads.
leo: Rough config sketch: 
```yaml
autoscalePolicy:
  preemptible: 
    stabilization_window: 60s
    initial_weight: 0.2
    max_weight: 1.0
    tenant_override_key: allow_preemptible_fallback
```
This could be plumbed through admission API.
sophia: Nice. Also let's include a cooldown penalty: if tenant got evicted from preemptible -> add short deny period for preemptible routes to same tenant to avoid thrash.
ops-bot: Deployment note: linked doc created <https://go/redwood/dedicated-preemptible-handshake> (internal).
mike: One more edge: bursting with mixed GPU types (A100 + T4) — packing decisions can force eviction when the autoscaler strips preemptible types first. Maybe admission should prefer homogeneous allocations and only mix when fragmentation unavoidable.
anya: That suggests allocator needs to report a "mix penalty" and autoscaler should factor placement frag. Could be an incremental change.
leo: Action items: 1) propose RFC for preemptible weighting + tenant QoS (I can draft), 2) add stabilization_window field to admission API, 3) add eviction-cooldown marker in tenant state. Anyone want to own the RFC?
sophia: I can co-author with you, leo. I'll add sample telemetry we need (eviction_rate_by_tenant, preemptible_ramp_up_time, mix_penalty_hits).
mike: Perfect. Let's keep the initial rollout as a config flag behind a feature toggle. Low-risk rollout: staging -> limited tenants in prod -> all.
anya: Sounds good. One more: let's log an event when autoscaler treats preemptible capacity as >=50% of decision so we can alert on risky configurations.
leo: Will include that. I'll open the RFC PR today and @mike @sophia please review.
mike: Thanks — ping here when PR is up. :thumbsup:
